_why: UIV-B4 (docs/eras/uiv.md, machines 21 and 22, line 35): the ergosphere probe bay and the Penrose engine at Cygnus X-1, and the sled hull's assembler row. Penrose 1969: a split charge dropped into the ergosphere returns more energy than it carried; the best case is about 20.7% (Chandrasekhar). Cygnus X-1: spin a* > 0.9985 (Zhao 2021), mass 21.2 solar masses (Miller-Jones 2021).

recipes.name: kerr_probe
recipes._why: UIV-B4 line 35: the probe is dropped through the ergosphere and writes the Kerr metric on a 5D data crystal (kept); the probe burns up.

recipes.name: split_sled
recipes._why: UIV-B4 line 35: a sled hull is loaded with a charge and a compacted waste canister as ballast; the Penrose engine splits the charge in flight.

recipes.name: refit_sled
recipes._why: UIV-B4 line 35, the refit loop: the half-sled the engine recovers is reloaded with a fresh canister and charge. The hull is reused; only the charge and the ballast are new.

recipes.name: sled_hull
recipes._why: UIV-B4 line 35: the sled hull, plated on the bay's rail (a far-machine row: a plain assembler row would fall under the C-COMPLEX floor). The plates are carried out; nothing here is gathered.

recipes.name: relay_seed
recipes._why: UXV-B1 (docs/eras/uxv.md, the Kerr sling): a relay seed on a tungsten steel block as ballast is slung round the hole and leaves Cygnus X-1 already at speed: the launched seed the c8 and c9 jumps need from here. The Moon's laser launcher stays the way to the first three places.

recipes.name: penrose_drop
recipes._why: UIV-B4 line 35: the sled drops into the ergosphere, the charge splits, one half falls into the hole and the other returns with more energy than it left with: 8 A at UIV (268,435,456 EU/t) for 2,400 ticks. The Kerr chart (kept) times the drop.
